headline: Healey files bill with two-month gas-tax suspension and broader relief
dek: The supplemental budget would suspend Massachusetts' 24-cent-per-gallon gas tax for two months while also capping ticket fees, lowering projected electric costs and expanding maternal-health support.
body: Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey filed a supplemental budget bill on Sept. 23 that includes a two-month suspension of the state's 24-cent-per-gallon gas tax. The administration says the measure would give temporary relief to families, truckers and rideshare drivers facing higher fuel costs.

The bill also includes a proposal to cap ticket-resale prices and fees and ban speculative tickets, along with changes to how electric utilities purchase power for basic-service customers. The administration estimates those electricity changes could save ratepayers about $610 million.

Healey's filing sets aside $2.25 million for postpartum care and maternal mental-health support. It also includes $41.5 million for Department of Transitional Assistance caseworkers and technology upgrades intended to help people remain enrolled in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program.

The administration estimates the gas-tax suspension would reduce revenue by about $120 million. It says that cost would be covered with unbudgeted fiscal 2027 Fair Share surtax collections and would not interrupt transportation projects financed through the Commonwealth Transportation Fund.

The legislation would appropriate $2.24 billion in gross spending, or $1.46 billion after revenue offsets, as part of an effort to close fiscal 2026 with a balanced budget. The gas-tax suspension and the rest of the package still require approval from the Massachusetts Legislature.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Healey Files Massachusetts Gas-Tax Suspension Bill
seoDescription: Gov. Maura Healey filed a Massachusetts supplemental budget with a two-month gas-tax suspension, ticket-fee caps, electric-cost savings and maternal-health funding.
